data.cultural_impact: The name "Satyendra" holds significant cultural importance in the Hindu tradition. It is derived from the Sanskrit words "Satyam" which means truth and "Andra" which means possessor or bearer. This name reflects the value of integrity and truthfulness that is deeply ingrained in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Satyendra" signifies a connection to the divine truth. The name suggests that the individual is on the path of seeking and living the truth. In Hinduism, Satya or truth is considered one of the essential virtues and a key aspect of spiritual growth. The name is a constant reminder for the individual to stay true to their values and beliefs, and to strive for inner peace and self-realization.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Satyendra: Truth is the ruler (inner self) within us. This name signifies a deep commitment to honesty and integrity, encouraging one to uphold truth in every aspect of life.

vedic_reference.note: Named after Lord Indra, the god of rain, thunderbolt, and the sky in Hindu mythology. Satyendra is a synonym for Satyavak, a truthful and sincere person in Indian culture.

historical_references.reference: Satyendra Prasad was the last Raja of Jaisalmer from 1942 to 1949. He was the 27th Jaisalmer ruler and the last of the Rajput dynasty.

Satyendra Nath Trivedi was an Indian independence activist, politician and writer who was born in 1885 in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. He was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and was imprisoned several times for his activism.

modern_usage.modern_context: Satyendra is a common Hindu name meaning 'truth-rule' or 'truth-reign'. The name Satyendra is also associated with traditional values such as truthfulness and integrity, which are highly valued in these sectors.
